Thomas D. Westergaard is a Danish designer and founder of Ceremoni Studio, where he transforms the traditional candle into a kinetic sculpture. Instead of treating wax as a static object, he engineers candles that bend, twist, and weave together as they burn. Every prototype is tested through long time-lapse recordings to study the flame, the melting wax, and the structure, refining each design until movement and combustion become one. His work sits somewhere between industrial design, engineering, and performance. #art #artist #avantgarde #candles #timelapse

Artist Rachel Youn creates kinetic sculptures and installations that combine artificial plants, discarded consumer objects and mechanical devices to imitate the movements of living organisms. In Pretty Behavior (2026), Youn modifies a neck massager and connects it to an artificial orchid and leaves using metal hardware, chains and glass. Once activated, the machine makes the flower shake and move continuously, giving the synthetic plant an uncanny appearance of life. Youn frequently repurposes massagers and other machines originally designed to act on the human body, redirecting their repetitive movements into artificial plants. The objects appear to dance, struggle or react despite having no consciousness. #artist #art #niche #weird #avantgarde
